The '''Tokmia system''' was a [[Star system/Legends|star system]] in the [[Anoat sector/Legends|Anoat sector]], located in the [[Greater Javin/Legends|Greater Javin]] of the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]]. It contained the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Tokmia/Legends|Tokmia]].

==History==
Tokmia was one of several sites the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] suspected the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]] might have been hiding following the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]]. The [[Imperial II-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Imperial II''-class Star Destroyer]] ''[[Stalker/Legends|Stalker]]'', attached to [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader's]] [[Death Squadron/Legends|Death Squadron]], dispatched a [[Viper probe droid/Legends|Viper probe droid]] to the system in [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]] in search of the hidden [[Echo Base/Legends|Rebel base]].<ref name="GG3">[[Galaxy Guide 3: The Empire Strikes Back (Second Edition)|''Galaxy Guide 3: The Empire Strikes Back'', Second Edition]]</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
Tokmia was first mentioned in the [[The Empire Strikes Back: The National Public Radio Dramatization|published script]] of [[The Empire Strikes Back (radio)|''The Empire Strikes Back'' radio drama]]. Captain [[Lorth Needa/Legends|Needa]] mentions it as one of the destinations for his ship's probe droids as they went in search of the Rebel base.<ref name="radio script">[[The Empire Strikes Back: The National Public Radio Dramatization|''The Empire Strikes Back'': The National Public Radio Dramatization]]</ref> That portion of the scene was cut from the final version of the radio drama,<ref name="Freedom's Winter">{{ESBRadio|Freedom's Winter}}</ref> but after the script's publication, other [[Star Wars Legends|Legends]] sources began to make mention of the system.<ref name="GG3" />
